root.body:
I’ll check which Simulation Lead runs ended, what they left on disk, and whether any of their changes were merged.


▸
2 tool calls
There was another host restart at 10:09:34 pm Makassar. That interrupted several runs, so the lower count does not mean they all finished. I found their commits and partial files still on disk; I’m checking which work completed and which is being recovered.


▸
1 tool call
The worktrees are still present. CUDA, WebGPU and backend changes remain on their branches; the recent commits on main contain review records. The WebGPU billing reconciliation finished before the restart. CUDA image preparation and saved-pool integration now have replacement recovery runs.


▸
1 tool call
They didn’t all finish. Another host restart at 10:09:34 pm interrupted several runs.

The three Simulation Lead runs I found were two recovery workers and a failure handler. The handler has since ended; CUDA image preparation and saved-pool integration are still running.

The work is on disk:

Work	What survived
CUDA	Committed preparation at ad54d494, plus the interrupted image-plan work card. Recovery resumed in the same worktree.
WebGPU	Billing reconciliation completed and committed at 1fd98c40. The suite did not run: the ledger still charges old reservations despite only 14.2¢ in observed bills.
Saved-pool backend	Deadline/authentication changes committed at a0a1cc78, plus a partial runtime-preparation script. Recovery is underway.
Pressure controls	Completed source packet exists on disk, uncommitted. Its review was interrupted.
No CUDA, WebGPU or backend worktree was merged into main during this interval. Their branches and worktrees remain present. The recent main commits added 15 review/evidence files.

So there are completed preparations, blocked work and interrupted work being recovered. The inspected commits and partial files survived; this drop in worker count does not mean CUDA or beta is finished.


You
10:19 PM
wait a host restat? On unleashd? It shouldn't kill / rstat thread, does that mean we killed workers and lost their in progress work?


Wave Simulation Lead
10:19 PM
I’ll verify what the platform recorded. The key distinction is whether it interrupted the worker’s execution, deleted its thread history, or lost files on disk.


▸
2 tool calls
Yes—Unleashd recorded those runs as interrupted by a host restart. I should distinguish that from confirmed process death: the records don’t prove every underlying worker process was killed.

What survived:

Commits and files on disk, including staged and uncommitted changes.
The thread/run records and earlier checkpoints.
Enough saved context to start the two recovery workers, which are running now.
In-memory work since the last saved checkpoint may have been lost. I cannot confirm every unfinished response or tool result survived.

There is also a concrete recovery failure: an automatic resume was rejected because the thread “already has an active writer.” That indicates an execution-ownership conflict; its exact cause is unverified.

Your concern is justified. This restart did interrupt work, and continuation was not seamless. We have recovered the inspected disk artifacts, but I should not have implied that restarting workers preserves every part of an unfinished turn.

----
